</user_query>"}]},{"role":"assistant","content":"# Fixing ConstraintLayout Not Found Error

The error occurs because the ConstraintLayout dependency is missing from your project. You need to add it to your build.gradle file.

Here's the fix:

1. Open your app-level build.gradle file and add the ConstraintLayout dependency:

```gradle:app/build.gradle
// ... existing dependencies ...
dependencies {
 // ... other dependencies ...
 implementation 'androidx.constraintlayout:constraintlayout:2.1.4'
}
```

2. After adding the dependency, sync your project by clicking "Sync Now" in the notification that appears, or by clicking on the "Sync Project with Gradle Files" button in the toolbar.

The latest stable version is 2.1.4, but you can check for newer versions if needed."}]}

</user_query>"}]},{"role":"assistant","content":"# Resolving the ID Reference Error

The error occurs because you're trying to reference the CheckBox with `@+id/checkbox_task_completed` in your TextView constraints, but the CheckBox itself is also using this as its id definition. In Android XML layouts, when defining a new ID, you need to use `@+id/`, but when referencing an existing ID, you should use `@id/`.

Here's the fix:

```xml:app/src/main/res/layout/list_item_task.xml
 <CheckBox
 android:id="@+id/checkbox_task_completed"
 android:layout_width="wrap_content"
 android:layout_height="wrap_content"
 app:layout_constraintStart_toStartOf="parent"
 app:layout_constraintTop_toTopOf="parent"
 app:layout_constraintBottom_toBottomOf="parent" />

 <TextView
 android:id="@+id/textView_task_title"
 android:layout_width="0dp"
 android:layout_height="wrap_content"
 android:layout_marginStart="12dp"
 android:textAppearance="?attr/textAppearanceListItem"
 android:textStyle="bold"
 app:layout_constraintEnd_toEndOf="parent"
 app:layout_constraintStart_toEndOf="@id/checkbox_task_completed"
 app:layout_constraintTop_toTopOf="@id/checkbox_task_completed"
 tools:text="Buy groceries for the week" />

 <TextView
 android:id="@+id/textView_task_due_date"
 android:layout_width="0dp"
 android:layout_height="wrap_content"
 android:layout_marginTop="4dp"
 android:textAppearance="?attr/textAppearanceListItemSecondary"
 app:layout_constraintEnd_toEndOf="@id/textView_task_title"
 app:layout_constraintStart_toStartOf="@id/textView_task_title"
 app:layout_constraintTop_toBottomOf="@id/textView_task_title"
 app:layout_constraintBottom_toBottomOf="@id/checkbox_task_completed"
 tools:text="Due: Apr 15, 2025" />
```

The fix changes all reference instances from `@+id/` to `@id/`. The `+` sign is only needed when defining an ID, not when referencing it."}]}

The error occurs because the package structure in your imports doesn't match the actual file location. Let's fix that:

```kotlin:app/src/main/java/com/example/todolist/ui/theme/tasklist/TaskListActivity.kt
// Update the package declaration - remove "theme" from the package path
package com.example.todolist.ui.tasklist
// ... existing imports ...
```

The issue is that your package declaration includes `theme` in the path (`com.example.todolist.ui.theme.tasklist`), but your file is likely expected to be in `com.example.todolist.ui.tasklist`. 

You need to either:
1. Update the package declaration as shown above to match your file structure
2. OR move your file to match the declared package path

The simpler solution is to update the package declaration since your imports and code are already referencing the correct structure."}]}
